standard_prerequisites.use: The affine-space characterization of relative pseudo-coherence (same chapter, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize implicitly via the companion result) and pullback of pseudo-coherent complexes (Cohomology, lemma-pseudo-coherent-pullback).

core_obligations: Set up the closed immersion into affine space and its base change.
Prove the derived base-change isomorphism of pushforwards stalk by stalk from tor independence.
Conclude via the pseudo-coherent pullback lemma.

proof_roadmap.step: Stalkwise identification of the two derived tensors.
Push the isomorphism into the characterization lemma.

difficulty_reason: For X -> S locally of finite type, E an m-pseudo-coherent object of D(O_X) relative to S, and a tor-independent base change S' -> S with X' = X x_S S', the derived pullback E' is m-pseudo-coherent relative to S'. The retained proof is written: localize to affines, choose a closed immersion i : X -> A^n_S with base change i', and identify the pushforward Ri'_*(Lg^*E) with L(g')^* Ri_*E via the base-change map on stalks; the pointwise verification displays the derived tensor comparison E_x tensor_{A} O_{X',x'} versus E_x tensor_{O_{Y,y}} O_{Y_i,y_i} and concludes equality from the tor-independence hypothesis (both sides localizations of the same derived tensor over O_{S,s}); the conclusion is then an application of the pullback-stability lemma for pseudo-coherent complexes on ringed sites (Cohomology, lemma-pseudo-coherent-pullback). Retained author proof at lines 17122-17152.
